message.content:
Based on my search, here are examples of preventive medicine practices organized by their levels of prevention:

## Primary Prevention (Preventing Disease Before It Occurs)

Primary prevention focuses on avoiding the development of disease entirely by addressing risk factors before any health issues arise.

**Lifestyle and Behavioral Interventions:**
- **Health education and promotion** – educating the public on healthy lifestyles, balanced diets, regular exercise, and avoiding tobacco and excessive alcohol
- **Smoking cessation programs**
- **Nutritional counseling** and promoting healthy eating habits
- **Regular physical exercise** programs
- **Stress management techniques** including yoga and meditation
- **Sunscreen use** to prevent skin cancer
- **Handwashing and proper hygiene practices**
- **Safe sex practices and contraception**
- **Fall prevention strategies** for older adults
- **Use of seatbelts** and accident prevention measures

**Immunization Programs:**
- **Childhood vaccinations** (measles, smallpox, polio, etc.)
- **Annual influenza vaccines**
- **HPV vaccines** to prevent cervical cancer
- **COVID-19 vaccines**
- **Lifelong vaccination strategies** based on age-related susceptibility

**Environmental and Policy Interventions:**
- **Improving air and water quality**
- **Creating safe sidewalks and urban planning** to promote physical activity (primordial prevention)
- **Environmental protection** to reduce exposure to harmful substances

## Secondary Prevention (Early Detection and Intervention)

Secondary prevention focuses on detecting diseases in their earliest stages, often before symptoms appear, when treatment is most effective.

**Screening Programs:**
- **Blood pressure screenings** – regular monitoring for hypertension
- **Cholesterol level checks**
- **Blood glucose tests** for diabetes and prediabetes detection
- **Cancer screenings:**
  - Mammograms for breast cancer
  - Colonoscopies for colorectal cancer
  - Pap smears for cervical cancer
  - Prostate exams
  - Low-dose CT scans (LDCT) for lung cancer in high-risk individuals
  - Skin examinations for melanoma
- **Vision and hearing tests**
- **Osteoporosis screenings** (DEXA scans)
- **HIV and STI testing**
- **Depression screenings**
- **Developmental screenings for children**
- **Tuberculosis skin tests**

**Regular Medical Check-ups:**
- **Annual physical examinations** – comprehensive health assessments
- **Well-child visits** – holistic examination of children's growth, development, and health needs
- **Prenatal care** – monitoring fetal development, screening for gestational diabetes, and preventing complications

## Tertiary Prevention (Managing Established Disease)

Tertiary prevention aims to reduce the long-term impact of chronic diseases, minimize complications, prevent disability, and improve quality of life.

**Disease Management and Rehabilitation:**
- **Cardiac rehabilitation** after heart attacks
- **Stroke rehabilitation** programs
- **Physical therapy** after orthopedic surgeries
- **Heart failure management**
- **Anticoagulation monitoring**
- **Continuous monitoring of chronic conditions** like diabetes to prevent nerve damage or kidney problems
- **Surgical valve repair or replacement** for rheumatic heart disease
- **Hypertension drug management**
- **Appropriate use of preventive medications** (statins, aspirin when indicated)

## Quaternary Prevention (Preventing Over-medicalization)

A newer category that aims to protect patients from unnecessary or excessive treatments:
- **Avoiding unnecessary imaging** in sports medicine
- **Ethical scrutiny of medical interventions** to ensure benefits outweigh harms
- **Preventing overdiagnosis and overtreatment**

## Innovative and Emerging Approaches

**Technology-Enabled Prevention:**
- **Predictive analytics** for early disease prediction (colorectal cancer, breast cancer, heart disease risk models)
- **Mobile health apps** (MyFitnessPal, Headspace) for tracking diet, exercise, and mental well-being
- **Wearable devices** (Fitbit, Apple Watch) for monitoring physical activity, heart rate, and vital signs
- **Telemedicine platforms** for virtual consultations and timely intervention
- **Electronic health records** for coordinated care

**Alternative and Complementary Approaches:**
- **Ayurvedic preventive practices** – personalized dietary and lifestyle interventions based on individual constitution (dosha)
- **Seasonal routine adjustments** for maintaining health balance

Sources:
1. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK537222/
2. https://mesafp.com/blog/what-is-the-best-example-of-preventive-care/
3. https://idcchealth.org/blogs/what-is-preventive-medicine-and-what-are-its-types/
4. https://www.scirp.org/journal/paperinformation?paperid=143897
5. https://www.msdvetmanual.com/public-health/principles-of-epidemiology/public-health-prevention-strategies
6. https://www.auamed.org/blog/what-is-preventive-medicine/
7. https://www.floridamedicalclinic.com/blog/preventive-medicine-examples-why-its-important/
8. https://www.preventivemedicinedaily.com/diseases-conditions/infectious-diseases/infectious-diseases-prevention-strategies-to-protect-public-health/
9. https://www.healthviewx.com/the-role-of-predictive-analytics-in-preventive-healthcare/
10. https://www.drishtiias.com/blog/ayurveda-for-preventive-healthcare
11. https://www.hilarispublisher.com/open-access/advancing-public-health-innovative-strategies-for-disease-prevention-and-control.pdf
